guidelines.detail: refines FID-01 (The description says accepting an offer makes all other offers no longer valid (S5), and the reference models this as a separate task (M10), but the generated model omits it. The arrival of offers is a wait and is correctly an intermediate catch event, so it is not a mistake to fix.)

same as LRN-022 (P4 is a combined 'Accept or deny offer' task where the description gives accepting and denying as separate choices. P1 is a single task label that lists four data items from one sentence, while the reference splits or narrows that step. Both are label-level divergences from the reference that come from merging several actions or objects into one task label. The records support the rule, but it lar)

refines GW-04 (M7 and M8 show that the reference places parallel gateways around the concurrent actions that follow accepting an offer, and the generated model has none. GW-04 already requires a parallel split when all branches start, but it does not say that explicit 'in parallel' wording in the description triggers it, or that the matching parallel join must follow. The proposed guideline keeps GW-04's rule of)

new guideline (Three label divergences share one cause: P2 drops the quantity and frequency constraint ('at least 3', 'every week') that the description attaches to the activity, so the task no longer says how often or how many. P4 replaces the description's state-change wording with a removal verb that the description never uses, changing the act. P3 shifts the label toward a selection step and away from the st)

refines FID-03 (FID-03 asks for short, faithful labels but does not say what to do when a label carries a quantity or frequency constraint. P5 shows the generated label kept the minimum count but dropped the period, while the reference keeps both. The guideline adds that constraints stated in the description belong in the label. The other label pairs (P1 to P4) are close paraphrases that the description supports,)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that choosing one of several pending alternatives makes the other pending alternatives no longer available: On the branch where the choice is made, model one task that withdraws the remaining pending alternatives, placed before the process continues. Do not leave this consequence implicit in the choice.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that choosing one of several pending alternatives makes the other pending alternatives no longer available

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states one sentence or step in which several distinct actions are chained on the same objects, or in which one outcome is delivered through alternative means (for example 'via X or Y'): Model each distinct action and each alternative means as its own task, in the order the description gives. If the description says one alternative is chosen, place the alternative tasks behind a decision gateway; if it does not choose, keep them as separate tasks on their own flow. Do not combine them into one task whose label lists them together.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states, in one sentence, a user action whose object is a list of several data items, or a choice between alternative actions on the same object

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that several follow-up actions after one activity are carried out in parallel (at the same time), and none of these follow-up actions depends on a condition: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one unconditional outgoing branch per follow-up action, with no decision conditions on those branches. Join the branches with a parallel gateway before any shared continuation, so the continuation waits for all of them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that several follow-up actions after one activity are carried out in parallel (at the same time), and none of these follow-up actions depends on a condition

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity whose verb is qualified by a quantity or frequency constraint (for example a minimum count or a repetition per period) that belongs to that same activity: Name the task with the verb the description uses for that act and keep the quantity or frequency wording that constrains it, in the description's language. Do not drop the constraint to shorten the label, and do not replace the stated verb with a synonym that names a different act or outcome, such as a removal verb where the description states a change of state.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity whose verb is qualified by a quantity or frequency constraint (for example a minimum count or a repetition per period) that belongs to that same activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an activity must be repeated with a minimum count within a time period, for example at least N times per period: Name the user task so that it keeps both the minimum count and the period as the description states them, and do not shorten the label to the activity alone.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an activity must be repeated with a minimum count within a time period, for example at least N times per period
